THE MEASUREMENT BEHIND THE MAP

Reading the observatory.

The observatory maps a selected collection of official US and EU statements. Positions use editorial source coding; the collection is not a complete historical survey.

What moves a planet?

Each document is assigned an explicit editorial label: supports Ukrainian sovereignty (+1), supports territorial revision (−1), or unclear (unscored). The planet’s coordinate is the equal-weight mean of the scored documents for that actor and year. Our current selected documents all express support: equal scores intentionally have equal horizontal coordinates.

score = sum(document labels) / scored documents
x = 6 × score

The anchors sit at x = −9 and +9. Vertical and depth offsets keep actors apart; only the horizontal coordinate carries meaning. Camera perspective can change apparent distance. Reset perspective to compare positions.

Missing is not neutral

Without scored documents, a planet appears in a separate lower observation lane marked “Unscored”. Its location is not a stance. No interpolation fills the historical gaps, and one selected document does not establish an annual national position.

Evidence before certainty

Highlights are explicitly chosen evidence passages. Summaries are editorial paraphrases. EU institutional statements are not separate measurements of all member states. Full original documents open on the issuing institution’s website; locally available US transcripts can also be read here.

Independent research project · No affiliation with HCSS or a government agency.
